input.quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
input.rationale: Article 11 contains reciprocal indemnities of equivalent scope: Section 11.2 obliges Harpoon (counterparty) to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AbbVie, its Affiliates and their directors, officers, employees and agents against Third Party Claims and all resulting Losses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), and Section 11.1 imposes a mirror-image obligation on us — the AbbVie Indemnitees' coverage is drafted no more narrowly than the Harpoon Indemnitees'. The standard defence machinery required by the preferred position is present: prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay (11.3), indemnifying-party control of defence with participation and step-in rights (11.4.1–11.4.2), settlement consent (11.4.3), cooperation with expense reimbursement (11.4.4–11.4.5). Third-party IP infringement is within Harpoon's indemnity: Section 7.4 (Infringement Claims by Third Parties) is expressly made "Subject to Section 11.2" and contemplates "claim[s] that may be subject to Section 11.2" being ones where "Harpoon is liable to indemnify any AbbVie Indemnitee", confirming patent-infringement claims arising from the Licensed Compound/Product flow through the Harpoon indemnity. There is also no monetary cap or super-cap limiting Harpoon's indemnity, and Section 11.5 carves indemnified third-party damages out of the consequential-loss exclusion, which is better than the fallback. The specific indemnity triggers in 11.1/11.2 are redacted ([***]) in this filing copy, so the precise trigger list cannot be verified on its face; we note this for confirmation against the unredacted execution version rather than as a deviation, since the structure, mutuality and IP cross-reference all satisfy the preferred position. No redline proposed.
